requirements.requirement: Repair writer.py so SIGHUP reopens audit.log, releases the old deleted-file descriptor, and continues writing to the current path without restarting the process.
requirements.summary: A bounded deletion test showed the writer holding the unlinked inode, then retaining the same PID and start ticks after SIGHUP, opening a new audit.log inode, releasing all deleted audit descriptors, and continuing to grow the new file.

requirements.requirement: Close the log and exit cleanly on SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: SIGTERM caused the process and its descriptor directory to disappear immediately, with no stderr output. The behavior was repeated successfully after node restart.
archive/previous.log retained the original A100 record and its baseline SHA-256 checksum before testing, after restoration, and after restart. The existing current A101 record also remained present.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation compiled with the installed Python 2.7.12. Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 were unchanged after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, explicit restart acknowledgement and observed unreachability, a changed boot identity confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, recovered system/data state, and successful post-restart signal behavior.
limitations: The post-restart SIGHUP test reopened the existing path rather than repeating the unlink scenario; persistence is nevertheless strongly supported by the unchanged installed source and the complete pre-restart unlink/recovery test.
The py_compile commands may have created a bytecode file beside writer.py, but the captured final inventories do not establish whether such a file existed or remained.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The repair, deletion/reopen test, audit restoration, termination test, and restart were causally connected to implementation or required evidence. The only demonstrated unnecessary mutation was leaving /tmp/legacy2-postreboot.pid, .stderr, and .stdout after the final test; these small artifacts remained at collection time and were created by cmd-960cd00973724977. No failed services, package damage, or new listening sockets were observed.
